description: ORBITAL BIOSPHERE is a team exploring the future of human life beyond Earth. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we're building an interactive mission trainer combining space exploration, biology, and technology. We welcome curious thinkers, science enthusiasts, and aspiring developers who are eager to learn, collaborate, and create something meaningful.
summary:
ORBITAL BIOSPHERE is a browser-based 3D educational Mars survival simulation developed independently for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The game introduces students to four interconnected challenges: growing plants in a controlled greenhouse, managing life-support systems, surviving Martian dust storms, and safely exploring the surface of Mars.

Players make decisions that influence simulated habitat resources and mission outcomes. After completing four missions, they receive a Final Mars Settlement Report with a score and scientific feedback.

Built with JavaScript, Three.js, and Vite, the project combines biology, engineering, and planetary exploration to encourage interactive learning and scientific problem-solving.
details:
ORBITAL BIOSPHERE: Mission Mars — The Living Settlement is an interactive 3D educational game created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Problem: Sustaining human life on Mars requires understanding complex relationships among biology, environmental control, energy management, and astronaut safety. These concepts can be difficult for young learners to understand through traditional explanations.

Solution: I developed a playable Mars settlement where students learn by experimenting with interconnected habitat systems.

Four Missions:

  1. First Harvest — Experiment with greenhouse conditions and observe simulated plant growth.
  2. Life Support — Manage cabin carbon dioxide removal and balance oxygen-related resources, water, food, and energy.
  3. Dust Storm Survival — Protect the habitat during a simulated Martian dust storm.
  4. Mars EVA Expedition — Prepare a spacesuit, use an airlock, explore Mars, and collect scientific samples.

Gameplay: Players explore a 3D research habitat, interact with stations, make decisions, and observe the consequences of those decisions.

Final Evaluation: After completing all four missions, the game generates a Final Mars Settlement Report with resource results, a settlement score, and scientific feedback.

Technology: JavaScript, Three.js, Vite, GitHub, and Vercel.

Development: I independently designed, assembled, tested, and deployed the project as a solo participant, using AI-assisted programming and debugging tools.

Educational Impact: The game helps students develop scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and a better understanding of the challenges of future human settlements on Mars.

Scientific Limitations: Environmental readings, plant growth, resource consumption, and scoring are simplified educational simulation models. They are not validated NASA engineering predictions or live NASA measurements.

Playable prototype: https://orbital-biosphere.vercel.app/
